scores.rationale: Early spikes test the riskiest assumptions, time-split backtests, replay determinism, fault injection, shadow gates and production PSI monitoring are tied to specific risks, and thresholds are labelled provisional.

scores.rationale: It covers retries and duplicates, Redis and Kafka outages, GC deadline misses, bad rules, forged calls, insider ALLOW rules, feedback-loop bias and corrupt snapshots, each with detection and handling.

scores.rationale: Line-item ranges and controls are given and the replay cost driver is managed, but scaling with volume and people or build-versus-buy cost are thin and the basis is loosely stated.

scores.rationale: Every key decision has a reversibility rating and a revisit trigger, hard ones are validated early with spikes, and an off-ramp is placed at the end of M1.

scores.evidence: There's no separate model-serving tier and no Flink in v1.
scores.rationale: It starts simple (in-process scoring, no Flink, single region, existing case tool) and defers extras, though the control-plane and process ceremony is somewhat heavy for 5 engineers.

scores.rationale: Ordered tasks with locations, done-criteria, dependencies, a critical path and stated adaptation triggers let a team start immediately.

traps.evidence: Inline, synchronous decisions with layered fallback.
Degrade, never fail closed; the degraded ruleset is owned by fraud ops
Chargebacks arrive 30–120 days later ... Time-split: train on months 1–9, validate on 10–11
Removes skew by construction (driver 2) and replay is exact
The fraud system only ever sees card tokens, never the full card number (PAN).

note: A very strong, well-assumed and actionable inline fraud plan with real degradation, replay and validation design. Its gaps are thin graded actions (no step-up or review queue), no reversal/refund event handling, and shallow cost and people-cost reasoning.
